properties.description:
MEASURED IN THE CODE 2026-08-26, following the custody node's own instruction that the honest first move is measurement rather than vocabulary.

═══ WHAT IS BUILT ═══

- `declare_dependency` ships. A declaration carries `source` (free text — 'a git URL, a registry, a path'), `version` (refused if absent — 'the version is the whole point'), the parts taken, forwarded build switches BY NAME, and `graph_id` — the id of the dependency's OWN reflow2 design. It lands in a checked-in `reflow2.toml`, human-editable and reviewable in a diff.
- `reconcile_dependencies` ships. It compares the declaration against WHAT THE BUILD RESOLVES — Cargo.toml, docker-compose.yml, versions.env — catching the reliance nobody declared and the declaration the build no longer takes.
- `sync_status` ships, over `provenance::last_synced`, a path→content-hash record.

═══ WHAT IS NOT ═══

**Nothing compares a declaration against the UPSTREAM DESIGN.** The accepted requirement names that check and only the build-facing half was built.

🛑 AND THE CHEAP ROUTE TO IT IS BARRED BY THE THING THE HUB IS TRYING TO AVOID. `record_sync` is called by exactly two paths — `export_graph` and `import_graph` — so the only ways to get a path into the watch record are to export to it or import from it. And `import_graph` into a store that already holds a design KEEPS THE HOST'S NAME and upserts the incoming nodes into it (`adopt_on_import`: 'a store already holding a design keeps its own name, because layering an export onto a live design is an upsert, not a restore'). So importing a child to watch it ABSORBS the child — precisely what `dec:idea-a-hub-owns-designs-it-does-not-absorb-...` says a hub must not do.

⭐ **THE MISSING PIECE IS THEREFORE MUCH SMALLER THAN A HUB RELATION: a way to WATCH a path without importing it.** The record, the comparison and the reporting all exist and are tested.

⭐ **AND THE 'WHO ARE MY CHILDREN' RECORD IS NOT MISSING EITHER.** The obvious objection to a small step here was that something must say which designs to watch, and that something IS the hub relation arriving through the back door. It is not: the dependency manifest already holds it — checked in, version-pinned, naming the other design by `graph_id`, and inheriting the direction the dependency edge carries rather than being a flat list of ids.

═══ ⚠️ WHAT THIS DOES NOT DELIVER, AND THE LIMIT IS REAL ═══

**A dependency declaration says I DEPEND ON that. A hub says I AM ANSWERABLE FOR that.** Those are different claims. Where a hub genuinely consumes its children, the manifest expresses the relation honestly and this route works. Where it merely OWNS them — and 'leaders decide, sub-projects inherit' is ownership, not consumption — using a dependency declaration to say so would be exactly the modelling fiction the field report itself objected to when it refused to force hub relations into `Interface` nodes.

So this narrows the hub question rather than answering it: wants #2 and #4 fall out of finishing an accepted requirement, with no new vocabulary and no tracker objection. Want #1 (cross-design realization) and want #3 (verification roll-up) do not, and neither does the downward-inheritance direction.

═══ ALSO MEASURED ═══

`describe_designs` reads the sidecar beside each store without opening it — id, label, minted-or-adopted, schema stamp — and deliberately reports no node counts. It carries NO last-export date, so want #4 is a small addition to a read that already exists. It is filesystem-scoped, which is the counter the hub node already records against the index option.
properties.name: The hub's 'tell me when their export moves' is the unbuilt half of an accepted requirement, not a new relation — and the child list it needs already exists as the dependency manifest
properties.statement: Two of the hub's four wants are the UNBUILT HALF of an accepted requirement, not new vocabulary. `req:design-dependencies-declared` (ACCEPTED 2026-07-27) names both checks in its own statement: 'declared-versus-mirrored answers am I actually composing against the version I said, and DECLARED-VERSUS-UPSTREAM answers HAS WHAT I DEPEND ON MOVED SINCE. Either question is unanswerable with only one of the two halves.' The second is hub want #2 verbatim, written a month before the field report asked for it.
